review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–74). The only nontrivial proof is `curtisEval_foldl`. Its two branches, `k/2 < 8` and not, share only routine `getD`/`ofFn` unfolding, and they sit inside one proof. Pulling that into a helper would just move duplicated branches into a helper, which the rubric says is insufficient. `decodeWord_cons_some` and `decodeWord_cons_none` are one-line simp wrappers. `curtisEval_ofFn`, `lift_eq_one_of_curtisEval`, `curtisToGroup`, `curtisToGroup_of` and `curtisToGroup_surjective` are short and each used once, with no repeated reasoning. I grepped the repo for similar machinery. `Certificates/Kernel/Spor/PK/CertBridge.lean` has `decodeWord_cons_of_lt` and `decodeWord_cons_of_not_lt`, but they decode `Int` codes (`evalCodes`), not the `ℕ`-coded `curtisEval` words here. That is a different structure, so it is not a repeated proof of this one. I did not open every grep hit, so some uncertainty remains about similar proofs in the large repository.
